subject: general
question: Find the value of (sin² 68^circ + sin² 22^circ)/(2(cos² 17^circ + cos² 73^circ)).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify **complementary angles**: 68° + 22° = 90° and 17° + 73° = 90°.

Using **sin²θ + sin²(90°−θ) = 1**, the numerator becomes 1.

Using **cos²θ + cos²(90°−θ) = 1**, the denominator becomes 2(1) = 2.

Result = 1 ÷ 2 = 1/2.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (sin² 68^circ + sin² 22^circ)/(2(cos² 17^circ + cos² 73^circ))

**Formula Used:** sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ; sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

⇒ Numerator: sin² 68° + sin² (90° − 68°)

⇒ Numerator: sin² 68° + cos² 68° = 1

⇒ Denominator: 2 × [cos² 17° + cos² (90° − 17°)]

⇒ Denominator: 2 × [cos² 17° + sin² 17°]

⇒ Denominator: 2 × 1 = 2

⇒ Value = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, and tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

Pythagorean Identities

The most fundamental identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, which applies for all real values of θ.

Square Sum Shortcut

If A + B = 90°, then sin²A + sin²B = 1 and cos²A + cos²B = 1.</p
